new_findings.text: The audio blocker is not a wall. ffdec cannot open 113_Mobile_MusicResource and 122_Mobile_SoundResource because they are XOR-obfuscated BEFORE the SWF header; applying the shipped key schedule turns both into ordinary CWS v17 SWFs that inflate and parse. Each holds 13 DefineSound tags, all MP3, 11025 Hz, 16-bit, mono, each bound to a SymbolClass name: music bgm_lose 3.53s, safepercussion/safekoto/safeambience 80.01s each, bgm_levelup 29.78s, bgm_gangnam 3.63s, flutes 80.01s, dungeonpiano/dungeonpercussion/dungeonflute/dungeonambience 45.74s each, battledrums 80.01s, battlechants 80.01s; sfx deflect 0.79s, die1 0.48s, die2 0.66s, die3 0.87s, slash1 0.35s, slash2 0.56s, slash3 0.27s, hitmetal 0.52s, punch 0.31s, sumo 2.90s, refund 0.73s, goodkoto 1.57s, fart 0.42s. The stem structure is itself a design fact: the 'safe' and 'dungeon' beds are 4 and 4 co-length stems (80.01s and 45.74s) - layered adaptive music, not single tracks. I did NOT listen to or grade any of it; I read tag headers only.

new_findings.text: The per-background override vocabulary in 123_Mobile_BGData is 22 tags, not the four the packet lists, and three of the overrides break the default ladder in ways the defaults cannot predict. Measured over all 49 rows: id 49, name 49, ffcount/fcount/ppcount/gcount/fgcount 49 each, wrap 17, contentwidth 17, fscroll 16, ffscroll 14, fblur 11, fwrap 11, ppwrap 9, ppblur 9, ffwrap 8, ppscroll 6, fgscroll 3, ffblur 3, gscroll 2, fgblur 2, gblur 1. Two rows set <gscroll>0</gscroll> - a LOCKED ground plane; three rows set <fgscroll>1.2</fgscroll>, overriding the 2.0 foreground ladder value; one row sets <ffscroll>1</ffscroll>, collapsing the farthest plane onto the camera. <gwrap> and <fgwrap> are never authored, and neither is <groundy> or <flatground>.

new_findings.text: groundY = 400 and flatGround = true are not per-background defaults that locations override - they are global constants for every location in the game. XMLBG's constructor overrides each field only when the matching tag is present (<groundy>, <flatground>), and across all 49 <bg> records in 123_Mobile_BGData neither tag occurs even once. The same is true of <gwrap> and <fgwrap>, so groundLayerWrap and foregroundLayerWrap are universally 1600.
new_findings.cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android_payload/scripts/XMLBG.as:10 (groundY=400), :12 (flatGround=true), :58-140 (override-if-present constructor) against the full tag histogram of reference/extracted/android/123_Mobile_BGData.bin (49 records, zero groundy / flatground / gwrap / fgwrap tags)
new_findings.lane_impact: L6 art-anim + L5 combat-core. A single authored ground line at y=400 for every scene in the game is a hard layout constant a recreation can bake in, and it is stronger than the banked reading of groundY as a mere default.
new_findings.quote: XMLBG.as:10 'internal var groundY:int = 400;' :12 'internal var flatGround:Boolean = true;' :66 'if(xml.groundy.toString() != "") { this.groundY = xml.groundy; }' - and <groundy> occurs 0 times across all 49 <bg> records.

new_findings.text: The <condition> evaluator's comparison enum is seven operators, not the two the packet names. StatsManager.checkCondition special-cases 'rand' first and then runs a full switch: eq, gte, gt, lt, lte, not, with default returning false. Authored usage across the whole Android corpus is 13 sites: nodedata rand x1; achievementdata not x1; questdata eq x5, gt x1, gte x2, not x1; uidata gte x1, lt x1, not x1. An absent <comp> defaults to 'gte'. Every <condition> in nodedata, questdata, uidata and achievementdata draws on the same evaluator, so any of them can be made probabilistic, negated or bounded.
new_findings.cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android_payload/scripts/StatsManager.as:4222 (rand), :4279-4295 (switch eq/gte/gt/lt/lte/not/default), :4173 (default gte); authored <comp> census over reference/extracted/android/*.bin
new_findings.lane_impact: L4 enemies-ai, L1 world-exploration, L-quests-story, L-economy. The ledger treats conditions as flat 'has item X' gates; the shipped evaluator is a six-operator comparison plus a probability primitive, and 'lte' is declared but never authored.
